questions.question: The incorporation of carbon into life-forms takes place through:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Photosynthesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Carbon** is the fundamental structural element of all known life, forming the essential backbone of complex molecules such as **DNA**, **RNA**, **proteins**, and **lipids**.
 
• The incorporation of carbon into the biological world occurs primarily through **Photosynthesis**, a physiological process where **inorganic carbon dioxide** (CO₂) from the atmosphere is 'fixed' into **organic molecules**.
 
• This biological transformation is driven by **photoautotrophs**, including **terrestrial plants**, **algae**, and **cyanobacteria**, which represent the base of the **trophic pyramid**.
 
• Within the **chloroplasts** of these organisms, the enzyme **RuBisCO** facilitates the binding of CO₂ to an organic sugar during the **Calvin Cycle** (light-independent reactions).
 
• The chemical energy required for this fixation is derived from **ATP** and **NADPH**, which are synthesized during the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis.
 
• The chemical summary for this conversion is: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O + solar energy → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂.
 
• Once carbon is incorporated into **glucose**, it is used to build plant tissues, which are then consumed by **heterotrophs**, thereby moving carbon through the entire **food chain**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Respiration**:

 
 
• This is a **catabolic process** occurring in the **mitochondria** where organic molecules are oxidized to release energy.
 
• It results in the release of **carbon dioxide** as a byproduct, making it an output phase of the **carbon cycle** rather than an incorporation phase.
 
 
 
• **Decomposition**:
 
 
• Carried out by **decomposers** or **saprotrophs** like **fungi** and **bacteria**.
 
• This process breaks down the complex carbon compounds of dead matter, recycling nutrients and returning **CO₂** to the atmosphere or soil.
 
 
 
• **Fermentation**:
 
 
• An **anaerobic** pathway used by organisms like **yeast** to extract energy from carbohydrates in the absence of oxygen.
 
• It involves the breakdown of sugar into **ethanol** or **lactic acid** and **carbon dioxide**, rather than the initial entry of carbon into life-forms.

questions.question: The Kalbelia dance is inspired by the movements of which animal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Snake**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Kalbelia dance** is a world-renowned folk dance originating from the state of **Rajasthan**, India, specifically associated with the **Kalbelia tribe**.
 
• The dance is a creative celebration of the tribe's traditional occupation as **snake charmers**, where every movement is designed to mimic the **graceful**, **slithering**, and **sinuous** motions of a **snake** or **cobra**.
 
• The performers, primarily women, wear heavy **black skirts** (Lehenga) decorated with **silver embroidery** and **mirrors** that swirl rhythmically, resembling the **shimmering scales** of a serpent.
 
• The choreography involves **flexible body movements**, **acrobatic bends**, and **swirling spins** that intensify as the music's tempo increases, mirroring the **agile** nature of a reptile.
 
• In **2010**, the **Kalbelia** folk songs and dances were inscribed on the **UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**, recognizing its cultural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Musical Instruments:**

 
 
• The most critical instrument is the **Pungi** (or Been), a wind instrument traditionally used to **charm snakes**, which provides the soul of the performance.
 
• Other accompanying instruments played by the men include the **Dafli**, **Khanjari**, **Dholak**, and **Khuralio**.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• The **Kalbelia community** is also known as **Saperas** or **Jogis**; they were traditionally nomadic and known for catching **venomous snakes** and trading their venom.
 
• Due to the **Wildlife Protection Act of 1972**, the tribe moved away from snake handling towards **professional dance** and music to preserve their cultural identity.
 
 
 
• **Prominent Personalities:**
 
 
• **Gulabo Sapera** is a legendary dancer who is credited with bringing the **Kalbelia dance** to the **international stage** and earning it global acclaim.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is considered especially sacred for taking a holy dip on Mauni Amavasya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ganga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mauni Amavasya** is observed on the **Amavasya** (new moon day) of the Hindu month of **Magha**, which typically falls in **January** or **February**.
 
• It is considered one of the most auspicious days in the **Hindu calendar**, believed to be the day when the universe was created and the first day of the **Krita Yuga**.
 
• Taking a holy dip in the **Ganga** on this day is believed to cleanse a person of all sins and lead them toward **Moksha** (salvation).
 
• The primary ritual involves **Mauna Vrata**, a vow of silence, which devotees maintain throughout the day to focus on inner peace and spiritual discipline.
 
• The **Triveni Sangam** in **Prayagraj**, where the **Ganga** joins the **Yamuna** and the invisible **Saraswati**, is the most significant site for this ritual, especially during the **Kumbh Mela** or **Magh Mela**.
 
• Ancient scriptures suggest that on the day of **Mauni Amavasya**, the water of the **Ganga** turns into **Amrit** (divine nectar).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Significance of Other Options**:

 
 
• **Yamuna**: While the **Yamuna** is a sacred river and part of the **Triveni Sangam**, the specific merit of the **Magha** ritual is traditionally centered around the **Ganga**.
 
• **Godavari**: Known as the **Dakshin Ganga**, it is the most sacred river of **South India**. It is central to the **Pushkaram** festivals but is not the primary focus of **Mauni Amavasya** traditions.
 
• **Saraswati**: A mythical river mentioned in the **Rigveda**, it is believed to flow underground and meet the other two rivers at **Prayagraj**, adding to the spiritual potency of the **Sangam** bath.
 
 
 
• **Key Rituals**:
 
 
• Devotees often perform **Tarpan** (offerings to ancestors) on the banks of the **Ganga** after the holy dip.
 
• Donating items like clothes, food, and **Til** (sesame seeds) to the needy is considered highly virtuous on this day.

questions.question: The term "light year" is best defined as:

options.text: Time taken by light to cover distance in one hour
Distance light travels in one year
Speed of light multiplied by time
Time taken by Earth to complete one orbit

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Distance light travels in one year**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **light-year** is a unit of **astronomical distance** used to express the vast spans between celestial objects in space.
 
• It is defined as the total distance that **light travels in a vacuum** in one **Julian year**, which consists of **365.25 days**.
 
• Since light travels at a constant speed of approximately **299,792,458 meters per second** (roughly **3 × 10⁸ m/s**), a light-year equals about **9.46 trillion kilometers** (9.46 × 10¹² km).
 
• In the field of **astronomy**, this unit is preferred over terrestrial units like kilometers because distances to stars and galaxies are so immense that using smaller units would result in unwieldy numbers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Related Astronomical Units:**

 
 
• **Astronomical Unit (AU):** This represents the average distance between the **Earth** and the **Sun**, approximately **150 million kilometers**.
 
• **Parsec (pc):** Short for **parallax second**, it is equal to approximately **3.26 light-years** and is used by astronomers to measure even larger distances based on **trigonometric parallax**.
 
• **Light-second/Light-minute:** These are smaller subdivisions; for instance, the Sun is about **8.3 light-minutes** away from Earth.
 
 
 
• **Common Misconceptions:**
 
 
• Despite containing the word **year**, a light-year is strictly a measure of **distance** and not **time**.
 
• The time taken for light to reach us from distant stars means we are seeing those objects as they appeared in the **past**.

questions.question: Which type of telescope is used to observe radio waves from space?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Radio telescope**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **radio telescope** is a specialized astronomical instrument designed to detect and collect **radio waves** from space, which have much longer wavelengths than visible light.
 
• The core component is typically a large **parabolic antenna** (dish) that acts as a collector, reflecting incoming radio signals to a central **receiver** or **feed horn**.
 
• These telescopes are essential for observing celestial objects that emit little to no visible light, such as **pulsars**, **quasars**, and cold **interstellar gas clouds**.
 
• Because radio waves can penetrate thick clouds of **cosmic dust** and the **Earth's atmosphere** with ease, these telescopes can operate effectively during the day and in overcast conditions.
 
• The development of **radio astronomy** allowed for the discovery of the **Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB)** radiation, providing crucial evidence for the **Big Bang theory**.
 
• Due to the long wavelength of radio signals, these telescopes must be physically much larger than **optical telescopes** to achieve high **angular resolution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Optical Telescope**:

 
 
• Designed to gather and focus electromagnetic radiation specifically from the **visible light** portion of the spectrum (approx. 400 to 700 nanometers).
 
• It includes two main sub-types: **refracting** and **reflecting** telescopes, used primarily for observing stars, planets, and nebulae.
 
 
 
• **Refracting Telescope**:
 
 
• Uses a **converging objective lens** to bend (refract) and focus light.
 
• Often suffers from **chromatic aberration**, where different wavelengths of light focus at slightly different spots, creating a color blur.
 
 
 
• **Reflecting Telescope**:
 
 
• Uses a **curved primary mirror** to reflect light to a focal point.
 
• Invented by **Sir Isaac Newton**, this design is the standard for modern professional astronomy because mirrors can be supported from the back, allowing for much larger apertures than lenses.

questions.question: What is the duration of a standard ODI (One Day International) cricket match, including breaks, in terms of innings?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Two innings, each lasting 50 overs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A standard **One Day International** (ODI) is a form of limited-overs cricket played between two teams, where each team is allotted a single innings to bat and bowl.
 
• The duration of a full match consists of **two innings** in total, with each innings strictly limited to a maximum of **50 overs** (unless a team is bowled out earlier).
 
• Each over consists of **6 legal deliveries**, meaning each side faces up to **300 balls** to set or chase a target score.
 
• The match is designed to be completed within a single day, typically requiring a total playing time of approximately **7 to 8 hours**, excluding weather interruptions.
 
• A mandatory **innings break** is provided between the two innings, which usually lasts for **45 minutes**, allowing players to rest and the pitch to be maintained.
 
• The team scoring the most runs at the end of their respective 50 overs (or upon bowling out the opposition) is declared the winner.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Historical Evolution**:

 
 
• The first-ever ODI was played on **January 5, 1971**, between **Australia** and **England** at the **Melbourne Cricket Ground** (MCG).
 
• Initially, World Cup matches (1975, 1979, and 1983) were played as **60 overs** per side. The format was reduced to **50 overs** starting from the **1987 World Cup** held in the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Format Comparison**:
 
 
• **T20 Internationals**: This format consists of **two innings** of **20 overs** each, lasting roughly 3 hours in total.
 
• **Test Cricket**: The longest format, involving up to **four innings** (two per team) played over a maximum of **five days** without a fixed over limit per innings.
 
 
 
• **Fielding Restrictions**:
 
 
• ODIs utilize **Powerplays** to regulate field placements. **Powerplay 1** (Overs 1-10) allows only 2 fielders outside the **30-yard circle**, while **Powerplay 2** (Overs 11-40) allows 4, and **Powerplay 3** (Overs 41-50) allows 5 fielders outside the circle.

questions.question: Which country hosted the 4th BRICS Summit in 2012?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **4th BRICS Summit** was hosted by **India** on **March 29, 2012**, at **Vigyan Bhawan** in **New Delhi**.
 
• This summit was historically significant as it was the first time **India** hosted the group of five major emerging national economies, including **Brazil, Russia, China,** and **South Africa**.
 
• The official theme for the **2012** summit was **'BRICS Partnership for Global Stability, Security and Prosperity'**, reflecting the group’s commitment to collective economic development.
 
• A major outcome of the summit was the proposal to establish the **New Development Bank (NDB)**, which was intended to mobilize resources for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in emerging markets.
 
• The summit concluded with the **Delhi Declaration**, which urged for a more representative international financial system and called for the urgent implementation of the **2010 International Monetary Fund (IMF)** quota and governance reforms.
 
• The meeting was attended by prominent leaders, including Prime Minister **Manmohan Singh** (India), President **Dilma Rousseff** (Brazil), President **Dmitry Medvedev** (Russia), President **Hu Jintao** (China), and President **Jacob Zuma** (South Africa).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brazil**:

 
 
• Brazil hosted the **2nd BRICS Summit** in **April 2010** in **Brasília** and later hosted the **6th Summit** in **Fortaleza** in **2014**, where the agreement for the **New Development Bank** was signed.
 
 
 
• **China**:
 
 
• China hosted the **3rd BRICS Summit** in **April 2011** in **Sanya**, which marked the inaugural summit for **South Africa** as a full member of the group.
 
 
 
• **South Africa**:
 
 
• After joining the group in **December 2010**, the nation hosted its first summit, the **5th BRICS Summit**, in **March 2013** in **Durban** under the theme of 'BRICS and Africa'.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Evolution**:
 
 
• The term **BRIC** was originally coined by **Jim O'Neill** of **Goldman Sachs** in **2001**; the first formal summit was held in **June 2009** in **Yekaterinburg, Russia**.

questions.question: Who was awarded the Padma Shri in 2025 for work with the Musahar community?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhim Singh Bhavesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhim Singh Bhavesh**, a prominent social activist from **Bihar**, has been conferred with the **Padma Shri** award in **2025** for his distinguished service in the field of **Social Work**.
 
• He is widely recognized for his tireless efforts spanning over three decades toward the empowerment and holistic development of the **Musahar community**, which is one of the most socio-economically marginalized groups in eastern India.
 
• His work primarily centers on improving **educational access** for Musahar children, eradicating **social stigmas**, and ensuring the delivery of **government welfare schemes** to the grassroots level.
 
• Through his advocacy, he has played a pivotal role in promoting **land rights** and **vocational training**, helping thousands of families transition from extreme poverty toward sustainable livelihoods.
 
• The recognition highlights the **Government of India**'s focus on honoring unsung heroes who work for the upliftment of the **Mahadalit** and underprivileged sections of society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Musahar Community:**

 
 
• The term **Musahar** is derived from 'mus' (rat) and 'ahar' (seeker/eater), reflecting their traditional occupation.
 
• They are predominantly found in **Bihar**, **Jharkhand**, and the **Terai** regions of Nepal, and are classified under the **Scheduled Castes** category.
 
• Historically, they have faced severe **social exclusion**, with literacy rates significantly lower than the national average.
 
 
 
• **Padma Awards 2025:**
 
 
• The **Padma Shri** is the fourth-highest civilian honor in India, announced annually on the eve of **Republic Day** (January 26).
 
• The 2025 list featured a diverse group of individuals recognized for their contributions in **Science and Engineering**, **Medicine**, **Literature**, and **Public Affairs**.
 
• The selection process is managed by the **Padma Awards Committee**, which is constituted by the **Prime Minister** every year.

questions.question: Which individual became India's 87th chess grandmaster in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harikrishnan A Ra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Harikrishnan A Ra**, a talented chess prodigy from **Tamil Nadu**, officially became India's **87th Grandmaster** in **January 2025**.
 
• The title was conferred by the **International Chess Federation (FIDE)** after he secured his **third and final Grandmaster norm** during the **Monte-Carlo Open** held in **Monaco**.
 
• To achieve this elite status, Harikrishnan crossed the required **live Elo rating of 2500**, a mandatory technical benchmark for all aspiring Grandmasters worldwide.
 
• His journey to the title involved consistent performances against high-rated international opponents, meeting the **FIDE** criteria of playing at least **27 games** across specific norm-granting tournaments.
 
• With this achievement, he continues the legacy of **Tamil Nadu** as a powerhouse of Indian chess, a state that has produced more than half of the country's Grandmasters, including the first one, **Viswanathan Anand**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grandmaster (GM) Title Requirements**:

 
 
• **Norms**: A player must achieve **three GM norms** in tournaments that meet **FIDE** standards regarding the number of participants, their titles, and their diverse nationalities.
 
• **Rating**: A minimum **FIDE rating of 2500** must be reached at some point during the player's career to finalize the title application.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Options**:
 
 
• **D. Gukesh** (Dommaraju Gukesh) became India's **59th Grandmaster** in **2019** at the age of 12, making him one of the youngest in history. He is widely recognized for winning the **Candidates Tournament 2024**.
 
• The name **Parag Jain** does not correspond to a recognized Indian Grandmaster in the current top-tier rankings as of the 2024-2025 period.
 
 
 
• **Indian Chess Milestones**:
 
 
• India's chess revolution began in **1988** with **Viswanathan Anand**. The pace of title acquisition has increased significantly, with the jump from 50 to 87 GMs occurring in less than a decade due to better coaching and **AI-driven** training tools.
 
• The **All India Chess Federation (AICF)** plays a pivotal role in organizing the **National Championships** and facilitating international exposures for rising stars like Harikrishnan.

questions.question: Kaziranga National Park is famous for which animal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**One-horned Rhinoceros**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kaziranga National Park** is located in the **Golaghat** and **Nagaon** districts of **Assam**, situated on the edge of the **Eastern Himalayan** biodiversity hotspot.
 
• The park is globally famous for hosting the world's largest population of the **Great Indian One-horned Rhinoceros** (**Rhinoceros unicornis**), which accounts for approximately **two-thirds** of their global numbers.
 
• It was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **1985** due to its unique natural environment and the presence of rare wildlife species that thrive in its grasslands and wetlands.
 
• According to the **2022 census**, the population of rhinoceroses in the park was estimated at **2,613** individuals, reflecting successful conservation efforts over the decades.
 
• The park comprises vast expanses of tall **elephant grass**, marshland, and dense **tropical moist broadleaf forests**, providing the ideal habitat for these megaherbivores.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Asiatic Lion**:

 
 
• This species is found exclusively in the **Gir National Park** and Wildlife Sanctuary in **Gujarat**, India.
 
• It is currently listed as **Endangered** on the **IUCN Red List** and is distinct from African lions by the skin fold along its belly.
 
 
 
• **Bengal Tiger**:
 
 
• **Kaziranga** was designated as a **Tiger Reserve** in **2006** due to its high density of tigers.
 
• While present in Kaziranga, they are primarily the flagship species of reserves like the **Sundarbans** and **Jim Corbett National Park**.
 
 
 
• **Elephant**:
 
 
• The **Asian Elephant** is one of the 'Big Five' of Kaziranga, and the park is a key part of the **Kaziranga-Karbi Anglong Elephant Reserve**.
 
• They are frequently sighted in the riverine floodplains of the **Brahmaputra River**.

questions.question: Which dam is built on the Sutlej River?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhakra Dam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhakra Dam** is a concrete gravity dam located on the **Sutlej River** in the **Bilaspur** district of **Himachal Pradesh**.
 
• It is the primary component of the **Bhakra-Nangal Project**, which is a joint venture of the states of **Punjab**, **Haryana**, and **Rajasthan** designed for **irrigation** and **hydroelectric power generation**.
 
• The dam creates a massive reservoir called the **Gobind Sagar Lake**, named after the tenth Sikh Guru, **Guru Gobind Singh**, which has a storage capacity of about **9.34 billion cubic meters**.
 
• Standing at a height of approximately **226 meters** (741 feet), it is one of the highest gravity dams in the world and was the highest in Asia at the time of its completion.
 
• The project was officially dedicated to the nation in **1963** by Prime Minister **Jawaharlal Nehru**, who famously described such large-scale engineering works as the **Temples of Modern India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagarjuna Sagar Dam**:

 
 
• Located on the **Krishna River**, it straddles the border between the **Guntur** district of **Andhra Pradesh** and the **Nalgonda** district of **Telangana**.
 
• It is recognized as the world’s **largest masonry dam**, featuring 26 crest gates.
 
 
 
• **Hirakud Dam**:
 
 
• Built across the **Mahanadi River** in **Sambalpur**, **Odisha**.
 
• It holds the distinction of being the **longest earthen dam** in the world, with a total length of **25.8 kilometers**.
 
 
 
• **Tehri Dam**:
 
 
• Constructed on the **Bhagirathi River** in the state of **Uttarakhand**.
 
• It is the **highest dam in India** and one of the highest in the world, reaching a height of **260.5 meters**.

questions.question: Two long parallel wires carry currents in the same direction. What happens between them?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**They attract each other**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to **Ampere's Circuital Law**, a current-carrying conductor generates a magnetic field around it. For a long straight wire, the magnetic field lines form **concentric circles** centered on the wire, as determined by the **Right-Hand Thumb Rule**.
 
• When two long parallel wires carry currents **I1** and **I2** in the same direction, the magnetic field produced by the first wire at the position of the second wire is **perpendicular** to the length of the second wire.
 
• The second wire, being a current-carrying conductor in an external magnetic field, experiences a **Lorentz force**. By applying **Fleming's Left-Hand Rule**, the direction of the force on the second wire is found to be directed toward the first wire.
 
• Similarly, the first wire experiences a force due to the magnetic field of the second wire, which is directed toward the second wire. Because both wires experience forces pulling them together, they **attract** each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Force Magnitude and Formula**:

 
 
• The magnitude of the **magnetic force per unit length** (f) between two parallel wires separated by a distance **d** in a vacuum is given by the expression: **f = (μ₀ × I₁ × I₂) / (2 × π × d)**.
 
• Here, **μ₀** represents the **permeability of free space**, which has a constant value of approximately 4π × 10−⁷ T·m/A.
 
 
 
• **Opposite Currents (Anti-parallel)**:
 
 
• If the currents in the two parallel wires flow in **opposite directions**, the magnetic forces acting on them will be directed away from each other, causing the wires to **repel**.
 
• This phenomenon is the fundamental principle used to define the **SI unit of current**, the **Ampere**. One Ampere is defined as the constant current which, if maintained in two straight parallel conductors of infinite length and negligible circular cross-section placed 1 meter apart in vacuum, would produce a force equal to 2 × 10−⁷ Newtons per meter of length.

questions.question: Launched in July 2025, PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana targets 100 low-performing agri-districts with an annual outlay of Rs. 24000 crore for ____ years.

The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **PM Dhan-Dhaanya Krishi Yojana** is a specialized agricultural intervention scheduled for launch in **July 2025**, aimed at boosting the productivity of the primary sector.
 
• The scheme specifically targets **100 low-performing agri-districts** across the nation, identifying regions where the current crop yield is significantly below the national average.
 
• A robust financial framework has been established for this initiative, featuring an **annual outlay of Rs. 24,000 crore** to support **modern irrigation**, **seed quality improvement**, and **mechanization**.
 
• The total duration of the program is fixed at **6 years**, ensuring that the **long-term structural reforms** required in these districts have sufficient time to manifest as measurable economic growth.
 
• By maintaining this **annual outlay** over a period of **6 years**, the total projected expenditure for the mission is estimated at **Rs. 1,44,000 crore**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Selection Criteria for Districts**:

 
 
• Districts are selected based on parameters such as **low cropping intensity**, **high dependency on monsoon**, and **limited access to credit**.
 
• The scheme aims to integrate these districts into the **national agricultural value chain** through better **market linkages**.
 
 
 
• **Key Objectives**:
 
 
• Enhancing **Soil Health** through the systematic distribution of micronutrients and organic fertilizers.
 
• Deployment of **Agri-Tech** solutions, including **drones** for pesticide spraying and **IoT devices** for moisture monitoring.
 
• Strengthening **Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs)** to improve the bargaining power of small and marginal landholders.

questions.question: What was the Mansabdar's military responsibility under Mughal empire?

options.text: Maintaining a specified number of cavalrymen

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Maintaining a specified number of cavalrymen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mansabdari system** was the administrative and military framework of the **Mughal Empire**, introduced by Emperor **Akbar** in **1571** to organize the nobility and the army.
 
• The term **Mansab** denotes a rank or position, and every officer in the Mughal service was assigned a dual rank: **Zat** and **Sawar**.
 
• The **Sawar** rank specifically determined the **military responsibility** of the Mansabdar, requiring him to maintain a fixed number of **cavalrymen** (soldiers on horseback) and horses for the imperial service.
 
• Mansabdars were required to bring their troops for regular inspection, where the **Dagh** system (branding of horses) and **Chehra** (descriptive rolls of soldiers) were used to prevent duplication and ensure military readiness.
 
• The number of cavalrymen maintained was crucial for the **expansion and defense** of the empire, as these troops formed the bulk of the Mughal fighting force during military campaigns.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rank Structure**:

 
 
• **Zat**: Indicated the personal status of the officer and determined his personal salary in the hierarchy.
 
• **Salary (Jagir)**: Most Mansabdars were paid through **Jagirs** (land revenue assignments), though some were paid in cash, known as **Naqdi**.
 
 
 
• **Incorrect Functions**:
 
 
• **Collecting Taxes**: While Mansabdars collected revenue from their assigned **Jagirs** to pay their troops, the primary responsibility for revenue administration lay with the **Amils** and **Zamidars** under the **Diwan**.
 
• **Administering Justice**: This was the specialized duty of the **Qazi** and **Mir Adl**, who interpreted **Sharia** and imperial decrees.
 
• **Land Distribution**: The **Diwan-i-Ala** was the head of the revenue department responsible for overall land records and the distribution of revenue assignments.

questions.question: Which national initiative promoting responsible tourism was launched by the Ministry of Tourism in December 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Paryatan Mitra & Paryatan Didi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Tourism**, Government of India, introduced the **Paryatan Mitra & Paryatan Didi** initiative in **December 2024** to enhance the tourist experience by transforming local citizens into **tourism ambassadors**.
 
• The program was piloted across several culturally significant locations including **Orchha**, **Gandikota**, **Bodh Gaya**, **Aizawl**, **Jodhpur**, and **Sri Nagar** to test community-based hospitality models.
 
• The initiative is deeply rooted in the philosophy of **Atithi Devo Bhava**, focusing on training frontline service providers like **cab drivers**, **hotel staff**, and **local vendors** in **soft skills**, **safety**, and **cleanliness**.
 
• A primary objective is **women empowerment** through the **Paryatan Didi** component, which encourages women to lead tourism activities such as **homestay management** and **cultural storytelling**, fostering **inclusive growth**.
 
• The scheme aims to promote **Responsible Tourism** by educating participants on **sustainability** and **heritage preservation**, aligning with the broader vision of **Viksit Bharat @ 2047**.
 
• By integrating **digital literacy** into the training modules, the initiative ensures that local stakeholders can leverage **technology** to improve **service delivery** and reach a global audience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dekho Apna Desh**:

 
 
• This initiative was launched to promote **domestic tourism** by encouraging citizens to travel within India and witness the country's rich **cultural diversity**.
 
• It includes a **pledge** where travelers commit to visiting at least **15 tourist destinations** across the country by a certain timeframe.
 
 
 
• **Incredible India 2.0**:
 
 
• This is an upgraded **global marketing campaign** aimed at promoting India as a **holistic destination** for international travelers.
 
• It focuses on **niche tourism products** such as **Wellness**, **Spiritual**, **Medical**, and **Adventure tourism** to increase **foreign exchange earnings** and tourist footfall.
 
 
 
• **Responsible Tourism**:
 
 
• A concept focused on minimizing negative **economic**, **environmental**, and **social impacts** while generating greater economic benefits for local people and enhancing the well-being of host communities.

questions.question: What is Project Akashteer?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Automated Air Defence Control**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Project Akashteer** is a significant technological initiative developed for the **Indian Army** to automate its **Air Defence Control and Reporting** processes.
 
• Developed by **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**, the project aligns with the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** vision, aiming to modernize and digitize the military's operational capabilities through indigenous technology.
 
• The primary function of this project is to integrate various **radars and sensors** across the battlefield into a single, unified digital network, providing a comprehensive **Situational Awareness** picture.
 
• It streamlines the **sensor-to-shooter** loop, allowing for the rapid detection, identification, and engagement of hostile aerial targets while ensuring seamless coordination between different units.
 
• The system is designed to operate in a **Network-Centric Warfare** environment, enabling commanders to make informed decisions in real-time by consolidating data from diverse geographical locations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**:

 
 
• A **Navratna Public Sector Undertaking (PSU)** headquartered in **Bengaluru**, functioning under the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• It plays a pivotal role in manufacturing advanced electronic systems for the Indian Armed Forces, including **sonar, radar, and communication** equipment.
 
 
 
• **Significance in Air Defence**:
 
 
• Automation through Akashteer minimizes the risk of **fratricide** (accidental engagement of friendly aircraft) by maintaining an accurate **Air Space Management** record.
 
• The system enhances the mobility and flexibility of **Air Defence** units, allowing them to maintain connectivity even while deployed in remote or high-altitude border regions.
 
• It serves as a force multiplier by optimizing the utilization of expensive assets like **Surface-to-Air Missiles (SAMs)** and **Anti-Aircraft Guns**.

questions.question: In April 2025, an affordable electro-fluidic device for preliminary screening of Sickle Cell Disease (SCD) was developed by which Indian research institute?

options.text: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research
All India Institute of Medical Sciences

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Raman Research Institute**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Researchers at the **Raman Research Institute (RRI)**, an autonomous institute under the **Department of Science and Technology (DST)**, developed a point-of-care, low-cost **electro-fluidic device** for the preliminary screening of **Sickle Cell Disease (SCD)**.
 
• The device utilizes the **resistive pulse sensing** technique, which measures variations in **ionic current** as individual red blood cells (RBCs) pass through a **micro-aperture**.
 
• It identifies sickled cells by analyzing their **mechanical stiffness** and **morphological changes**, as sickle cells are significantly less deformable than healthy, disc-shaped RBCs.
 
• This **affordable screening tool** is designed to provide rapid results, making it highly effective for use in **resource-limited settings** and rural areas where expensive diagnostic infrastructure is unavailable.
 
• The development supports India's **National Sickle Cell Anemia Elimination Mission**, which aims to eliminate the disease as a public health problem by the year **2047**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sickle Cell Disease (SCD):**

 
 
• It is a **genetic blood disorder** characterized by abnormal **hemoglobin S**, which causes RBCs to become rigid and **crescent-shaped**.
 
• These distorted cells can block **blood flow**, leading to severe pain, **organ damage**, and anemia.
 
• India has the **second-highest burden** of SCD globally, particularly prevalent among **tribal populations** in Central and South India.
 
 
 
• **Raman Research Institute (RRI):**
 
 
• Founded in **1948** by the Nobel Laureate **Sir C.V. Raman** in **Bengaluru**, Karnataka.
 
• The institute specializes in fundamental research in **Physics**, including Astronomy, Astrophysics, Light and Matter Physics, and Soft Condensed Matter.
 
 
 
• **Other Research Entities:**
 
 
• **Tata Memorial Centre (TMC):** A premier national institute for **cancer research** and treatment located in Mumbai.
 
• **Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR):** India's largest **research and development** organization operating a network of 37 laboratories.
 
• **AIIMS:** A group of autonomous public medical universities known for **clinical excellence** and medical education.

questions.question:
Which of the following is a shot played in a match of tennis?

I. Forehand II. Backhand
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both I and II**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Forehand** is a primary groundstroke in **Tennis** where the player swings the racket across their body with the palm of the dominant hand facing the direction of the stroke. It is widely considered the most powerful and versatile offensive weapon for most players, often utilizing grips like the **Eastern**, **Western**, or **Semi-Western** to generate significant **topspin** and pace. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• The **Backhand** is a fundamental stroke played on the opposite side of the body from the forehand, with the back of the hand preceding the palm during the swing. Players may employ a **one-handed backhand** for greater reach and variety or a **two-handed backhand** for increased stability, power, and better handling of high-bouncing balls. ***Hence, statement II is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Other essential shots and technical aspects of a **Tennis** match include:

 
 
• **Serve**: The overhead shot that begins every point, which must land within the opponent’s cross-court **service box** to be considered valid.
 
• **Volley**: A shot typically played near the **net** where the player strikes the ball before it bounces on the ground, used to finish points quickly.
 
• **Smash**: A powerful overhead stroke, similar in motion to a serve, usually executed in response to a high **Lob** sent by the opponent.
 
• **Lob**: A high, arching shot intended to pass over an opponent standing at the net or to provide the player time to recover their defensive position.
 
• **Drop Shot**: A delicate touch shot designed to land just over the net with minimal bounce, catching the opponent far back at the **baseline**.
 
• **Court Surfaces**: Matches are played on various surfaces including **Grass** (Wimbledon), **Clay** (French Open), and **Hard Courts** (Australian and US Open), each affecting the ball’s speed and bounce height differently.
